meta.title: lovearound — share love
meta.description: A small gesture of care can cross any distance. Send it to someone you hold dear, or to someone you haven’t met yet.
meta.og_title: lovearound — share love. Feel connected to the world.

hero.kicker: A platform that helps love find its way to people
hero.title:
Share love.
Feel connected to the world.
hero.lead: A small gesture of care can cross any distance. Send it to someone you hold dear, or to someone you haven’t met yet.
hero.text: lovearound is a way to send and receive signals of love. Everyone has their own Love ID. An anonymous signal arrives on a connected computer or device and gently reminds you: someone thought of you. No words, and no need to reply.

idea.title:
More love.
More connection between us.
idea.lead: A small gesture of care can cross a room, a city or an ocean. It can reach someone close or someone you’ve never met, and let them feel they’re not alone.
idea.text: Once you’ve received love, you can pass it on. To a friend, to family, or to someone on the other side of the world. That’s how one gesture becomes the start of a chain that connects more and more people.
idea.why_text: so love can travel more freely around the world, and we can feel connected to each other more often.

platform.title: Send it your way. Feel it everywhere at once.
platform.analogy: Your Love ID works like an email address: there’s only one, yet mail lands on your phone and your laptop at the same time. Signals work the same way: they reach everything you’ve connected. Only the sender is never shown.
platform.p1_text: From the app on your computer, with a button on your own device, or at random, to “Someone out there”.
platform.p2: No one will know it was you
platform.p2_text: A signal arrives without a name. We don’t keep who sent what to whom, so the recipient can never find out.
platform.p3_text: Connect as many apps and devices to your Love ID as you like. A signal reaches all of them at the same moment.
platform.p4_text: The API is documented and the apps are open source. Anyone can build their own device or app.
platform.sender_alt: Mia at her laptop taps the heart next to Sam’s name
platform.room_alt: Sam’s room in the evening: a laptop on the desk, Heart and a lamp on the nightstand, a pendant on the wall
platform.devices_label: What’s connected to Sam’s Love ID
platform.hint: Switch devices on and off: the signal only reaches the ones that are on.
platform.st_press: Mia taps the heart next to “Sam”
platform.st_fly: The signal flies off. The sender’s name stays behind
platform.st_done: The signal lit up everything that’s connected. Sam will never know it was Mia.
platform.st_none: Sam has nothing connected, so the signal has nowhere to land. Switch on at least one device.

how.title: Love ID — your address for love
how.s1_text: It appears the first time you sign in. Share your link so others can send you love.
how.s2_text: Pick someone close, or “Someone out there”. One tap can make someone’s day a little brighter.
how.s3_text: Receive signals on your computer or a connected device. Just feel that someone thought of you.
how.s4_text: Whenever you feel like it, send your own signal to someone close or someone new.

heart.title:
A little heart.
A link to the wider world.
heart.lead: Two devices, one Love ID: a heart that lives at home with you, and a pendant that’s always with you.
heart.alt: Heart — a small white heart that glows softly pink
heart.h_text: A warm heart you can hold, with no phone or computer needed — just Wi‑Fi and your Love ID. When someone sends you love, it softly glows and pulses. Touch it, and the love goes on.
heart.h_li1: Sits by your bed or on your desk
heart.h_li2: Works on its own, no phone needed
heart.h_li3: Receives love and sends it with a touch
heart.p_alt: A heart pendant on a fine chain
heart.p_h3: A heart to carry with you
heart.p_text: A small pendant on a fine chain. It pairs with your phone and is there only to receive: when someone thinks of you, the pendant quietly answers, right by your heart. To send love back, use your phone.
heart.p_li1: Always with you, around your neck
heart.p_li3: Receives only — send from your phone
heart.caption: Heart and the pendant are device concepts. The final design may differ.
heart.strong: Get one for yourself, or give it to someone you’d like to feel closer to.

devices.diy: Don’t want to wait? Build your own device
devices.diy_text: lovearound is an open platform: the API is documented, the apps are open source, and anyone can build their own device or app for Love ID. A lamp, a toy or a small screen on an ESP32 that responds to your Love ID. A step-by-step guide — from the first wires to the first signal.

moments.title:
When you want to give
a little warmth.
moments.m1_text: She lives in another city. Today you send her a small sign: “I’m thinking of you.”
moments.m2: To a friend before a big day
moments.m2_text: Before an exam, an interview or a performance. A quiet sign of support that needs no reply.
moments.m3: To yourself, when you need support
moments.m3_text: Share your link with friends. They don’t have to find the right words to let you feel cared for.
moments.m4: To someone on the other side of the world
moments.m4_text: You haven’t met yet. But one gesture can connect you for a moment and make someone’s day a little brighter.

app.title: Care at hand while you’re at your computer
app.text: The app for Mac, Windows and Linux lives in the menu bar or the system tray. Pick a person, send a signal and get back to your day. Love you receive shows up as a soft glow on your screen.

get.title: Where to start?
get.sub: Pick wherever is easiest for you to send from. It’s one account, so you can connect the rest later.
get.desk_text: The heart is always at hand — in the menu bar or next to the clock — and signals arrive gently, right on your screen.
get.linux: Ubuntu 24.04 or later, GNOME and KDE
get.web_text: Handy for sending from your phone: open it and tap.
get.tg_text: The @LoveAroundMeBot bot: send signals right from the chat and get them as notifications.
get.source: The apps are open source: code and every version are on GitHub.
get.support: Didn’t manage to install it? Write to us in the Telegram group, we’ll help.
get.smartscreen_text: That’s how Windows greets new programs that don’t have a publisher signature yet. Click “More info”, then “Run anyway”. The installer sets the app up just for you, without admin rights. The heart appears in the tray next to the clock; if you can’t see it, click the “^” arrow and drag it onto the taskbar.
get.linux_help_text: On Ubuntu, open the downloaded file and click “Install”, or run sudo apt install ./LoveAround.deb in a terminal. The heart appears in the tray. On GNOME, sign out and back in once after installing so the screen can glow; until then signals arrive as notifications.

faq.title: Everyone has a little love to share.
faq.q1: Will the person know it’s me?
faq.a1: No. The signal arrives with no name and no words — just a sign that someone thought of them. We don’t keep a record of who sent what to whom.
faq.q2: Do I need to buy the heart?
faq.a2: You can start with the desktop app. Heart will be an extra, physical way to receive signals.
faq.q3: Who gets a “Someone out there” signal?
faq.a3: A random member who has agreed to receive these signals. That way care can reach someone beyond the people you know.
faq.q4: Do I have to reply to a signal?
faq.a4: No. You can simply take in the moment. And when you feel like it, send a little love on.
faq.a5: Yes. You can already build your own device, for example on an ESP32, and connect it through the open API. Ready-made devices like lamps, bracelets, toys and small screens are in our plans, and we’ll add them step by step.
faq.a6: The app is free. We’ll share Heart’s price closer to launch.
faq.q7: What if the app won’t install?
faq.a7: Write to @lovearound_help on Telegram: say which system you have and what went wrong, a screenshot helps. We answer there, and other people’s questions may already have your answer.

end.title: Let’s bring a little more care into the world.
end.text: Start with one person. Or send a little love to someone out there.

footer.motto: Share love. Feel connected to the world.

invite.title: You’ve been sent a Love ID — lovearound
invite.og_title: You’ve been sent a Love ID on lovearound
invite.description: lovearound is a quiet way to say “I’m thinking of you”: one tap, and a warm signal reaches the person. Add this Love ID to send them one. They won’t know it’s you.
invite.kicker: You’ve been sent a Love ID
invite.h1: Someone wants you to be able to say “I’m thinking of you” — with a single tap.
invite.lead: lovearound carries small signals of love. You tap a heart, and the person’s computer, lamp or pendant softly responds. No words, no name, no need to reply.
invite.id_text: This is the address of the person who sent you the link. Add it, and you can send them a signal whenever you like. They won’t know it’s you.
invite.no_code: There’s no Love ID in this link. Ask for it to be sent again.
invite.where: Where would you like to add it?
invite.where_text: Pick wherever is easiest for you to send from. It’s one account, so you can connect the rest later — the Love ID stays put.
invite.desk_text: The heart is always at hand — in the menu bar or next to the clock — and signals arrive gently, right on your screen.
invite.desk_s2: Come back here and press “Open in lovearound” — the Love ID fills itself in
invite.installed_mac: Open LoveAround.dmg from your Downloads, drag lovearound into Applications and launch it.
invite.installed_windows: Run LoveAroundSetup.exe from your Downloads — lovearound will appear next to the clock.
invite.installed_linux: Open LoveAround.deb from your Downloads and click “Install” — lovearound will appear in the tray.
invite.add_after: Once the app is running, come back here and press the button. The link is already copied, so you can also just paste it into the app’s “Add” window.
invite.nothing_text: Then lovearound isn’t installed yet. Download it (step 1 above), then press “Open” again.
invite.desk_away: There’s an app for Mac, Windows and Linux. Open this link on a computer and you’ll find the Download button there.
invite.web_text: The web app opens with the Love ID already filled in. Works on your phone and your computer.
invite.tg_text: The @LoveAroundMeBot bot: send signals right from the chat and get them as notifications.
invite.anon: The signal arrives without a name: the person won’t know it was you.
